approach: Write x, y, z using the distance-in-the-nth-second formula, substitute into the given combination, and show it collects into two brackets that both vanish.

steps.text: The distance covered in the nth second of motion with constant acceleration a and initial velocity u is this.
Write x, y, z using this formula for n = p, q, r.
steps.equation: x = u + a(p − ½), y = u + a(q − ½), z = u + a(r − ½)

steps.text: Substitute into the given combination and group the u terms and the a terms separately.
The coefficient of u is zero because the three bracketed terms cancel in pairs.
Expand the coefficient of a; every term in p, q, r of degree two cancels, and the remaining constant terms also cancel, leaving zero.
steps.why_this_step: With both brackets zero, the whole expression (q−r)x+(r−p)y+(p−q)z equals zero, which is what was to be proved.

final_answer.value: (q − r)x + (r − p)y + (p − q)z = 0, proved by substituting the nth-second distance formula for x, y, z and showing both the u-coefficient and the a-coefficient vanish.

common_mistakes.text: Using the total distance formula sₙ = un + ½an² instead of the distance-in-the-nth-second formula sₙ = u + a(n − ½) leads to an expression that does not reduce to zero.
